newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa finmin mulls Transnet pension deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa finmin mulls Transnet pension deal - paper.

text.p: Finance Minister Trevor Manuel is considering a solution to the Transnet pension fund deficit would would not cost the taxpayer anything and which would pave the way for billions of rands in privatisation, Business Day newspaper said on Thursday.
The huge shortfall in the Transnet pension fund is blocking the way to bringing in private equity partners for some of its units.

A report containing the prosposals was written by a committee chaired by consultant Charles Stride and which included representatives from the goververnment's privatisation adviser HSBC and the finance department, the paper said.

A source said a key element of Stride's report was that it valued the shortfall at considerably less than the earlier estimates of 17 billion rand, which brought down the cost of reducing it by more than half.
It also recommended unbundling Transnet as a precursor to getting strategic equity partners for some of its subsidiaries.
Its key recommendation was to use the tax losses of the Transnet group as a means to address the shortfall.

By proposing that the new owners of Transnet subsidiaries pay a constribution to the pension fund -- instead of paying tax -- Stride had come up with a solution which would not affect the budget, a source said.
